title: fix: repair stale ClawHub plugin host links during doctor
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ClawHub-installed plugins keep an old OpenClaw host link after copying or upgrading a source-backed environment, so plugin validation can fail even after Doctor runs.

Related: [CLAW-911](https://linear.app/my-openclaw/issue/CLAW-911/repair-plugin-peer-link-portability-in-source-backed-upgrade).

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor --fix` now repairs the host link for registered ClawHub plugins using the same ownership checks as npm plugins. Read-only Doctor reports the problem; developer-owned installations and paths outside the authoritative plugin root remain untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared registry repair accepted only npm records, although both registries install through the same host-link owner. Include ClawHub records in that existing flow and use accurate operator-facing wording. Existing serialized health/action identifiers stay unchanged. Production change: 19 additions and 19 deletions; tests: 43 additions and 14 deletions.

## Evidence

- Before: the existing Doctor scenarios fail for ClawHub records; a copied-plugin case retains the old host link. npm cases pass.
- After: 47 focused Doctor/peer-link tests pass, including both registries, source byte/link preservation, read-only reporting, symlink escapes, developer-owned siblings, foreign packages, and unreadable packages.
- The built public CLI `openclaw doctor --non-interactive --fix` repaired an isolated canonical ClawHub record from the old host to this checkout, exited 0, and preserved the original host manifest. Full build and required changed checks passed; fresh independent review found no actionable issues.
- Published-updater compatibility: exact released `v2026.9.4` source `3a9d69db306c` with its frozen dependency graph ran its native `runGitDoctorStep` and default command runner against built candidate `4a17e999973a`. Its generated external-service policy invoked the candidate Doctor on canonical ClawHub state created by the released index writer. The link changed from the released host to the candidate; original host and plugin payload hashes, canonical install record, SQLite schema version 17, and all 104 table definitions were preserved. Exit 0; only fixture node-hosting advisories remained. This covers the changed updater-to-Doctor boundary and fulfills the requested ClawSweeper rank-up proof; whole checkout activation is still the later preflight.
- Final mechanical follow-through `ef8de8a6d3ab` corrects the post-update caller’s registered-plugin success/failure wording and private helper name. All 26 post-core convergence tests, the complete selected repository checks, and a fresh independent review pass. Repair control flow and serialized identifiers are unchanged; the published-driver boundary proof above remains applicable.
- A live, unmarked ClawHub package-metadata request returned HTTP 200. The earlier `ENOTFOUND` was observed during the real upgrade preflight and is not claimed fixed by this change.

The full work-environment upgrade preflight and live rollout remain pending; this proof does not claim that they succeeded. An unrelated local wrapper experiment modified generated dependency metadata and wrappers in the existing source checkout. The reviewed recovery restored 127 known files without installing, swapping the dependency tree, or restarting the live Gateway; 84 ESM imports and all 34 service states remained valid. Evidence and recovery limits are recorded in CLAW-911; this PR contains only the Doctor repair above.



ClawSweeper revision 3 follow-up — **Add data-model compatibility proof: addressed.** The released updater proof above compares the canonical install record, schema version 17 and all 104 table definitions before/after; each is unchanged, and the source/plugin payload hashes are preserved. This change expands the existing host-link repair eligibility only. There is no new schema, projection, retention, or persistence format to migrate. Whole-environment activation remains a separate preflight and is not claimed by this boundary proof.
